title: ⚡ “Compacting conversation…” small message, big impact on your session 🔄
summary: VSCode automatically compacts agent conversation history when the context window approaches its limit to maintain session continuity. You can manually control compaction with the /compact command or start a fresh session, balancing between preserving context and maintaining response quality.
key_points: Context windows are finite and fill up faster with agentic tool usage than simple chat
VSCode compacts conversation automatically when limits are reached, or you can trigger it manually with /compact
Manual /compact with instructions lets you guide what information gets prioritized in the summary
Quality may decline as context limit nears; alternatives include manual compaction or starting a new session

quotes.text: Quality may decline as limit nears
quotes.why_it_matters: Warns users that context compaction causes quality degradation, making it important to manage proactively

quotes.text: The context window is finite. As your session grows with messages, tool results, and instructions, the available space fills up.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains the fundamental constraint driving automatic compaction behavior in agent sessions

quotes.text: Manual control exists: /compact with optional instructions, so you guide what gets prioritized.
quotes.why_it_matters: Shows users can control compaction strategy rather than relying on automatic behavior alone
